independentReview.reason: APPROVE at the exact landing head, no blocking findings, with every claim checked by running commands rather than by reading the PR. The reviewer proved the new guard is not vacuous by breaking all three of its assertions deliberately: it emptied the delete command (failed with 'no refs parsed out of the delete command'), injected beta/private-beta-001 (failed naming the frozen beta ref), and parked an orphan commit at a fake refs/remotes/origin ref via git commit-tree to force the stranded-commit path (failed reporting 'lane/fake-orphan-test (+1)'), plus an unfetched name to force the 'unmeasured' branch. It verified the destructive command's own safety independently: 12 of the fifteen refs are ancestors of origin/main by merge-base --is-ancestor and three are not, at 151, 149 and 590 behind; beta/private-beta-001 is absent; and no open PR bases or heads on any of the fifteen, which is the #337 hazard that would silently shut somebody's PR. It confirmed the four repaired cap numbers first-hand and went further than asked by diffing the WHOLE doc-budget.ps1 between the two refs to check the argument was not hiding unique work -- it is not; 274 is strictly older in that file. It confirmed issue #351 is genuinely OPEN and that its body matches the disclosure. Its only non-blocking notes are pre-existing dependency advisories outside this PR's scope.
independentReview.priorReviewNote: A FIRST independent review examined head fe6bef98 and also returned APPROVE with no blocking findings. It is recorded here because it is the reason this head exists, NOT as proof of what lands. It found that the PR's prose and the shipped checklist both claimed two versions of scripts/doc-budget.ps1 'carry identical caps' when they do not -- origin/main caps docs/OWNER_ACTION_CHECKLIST.md at 385 lines / 32256 bytes and origin/lane/css-margin-separators-274 at 450 / 33792 -- and marked the finding explicitly NON-BLOCKING. The writer verified it first-hand and repaired it anyway rather than merging and filing it, because the false sentence sits in the section the owner reads immediately before running git push origin --delete, and 'a delete list is either true or it is a hazard' is this lane's entire premise. The corrected reasoning is also stronger than the sentence it replaces: 274 holds the OLDER, LOOSER cap that main has since ratcheted down, so restoring that ref would reintroduce a budget the ratchet exists to prevent, which argues FOR the delete rather than against it. The repair created commit 966b2895, which moved the head, so the first APPROVE does NOT cover what lands and is NOT being reused -- a second, fresh, independent review was commissioned at the new head and is the verdict this merge rests on.
